title: Scene Safety & Primary Survey (DRABC / ABCDE)
summary: Make the scene safe, check for a response, get help on the way, then check Airway, Breathing and Circulation. Use this first for every casualty.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} as soon as you know someone is seriously hurt or ill
when: The person does not respond to your voice or a gentle shake
They are not breathing, or breathing is not normal (gasping)
There is more than one casualty, or the scene is not safe (traffic, fire, fuel, electricity, water, chemicals)
You are unsure – it is better to call

steps.title: D – Danger
steps.text: Stop and look before you approach. Do not become a second casualty.
points: Traffic: park safely, hazard lights on, wear high-visibility clothing, warn oncoming traffic if you can do so safely
Fire, fuel, smoke, chemicals, electricity, water, unstable vehicles or structures
If it is not safe, stay back and call {EMERGENCY}

steps.title: R – Response
steps.text: Kneel beside them, gently shake their shoulders and ask loudly: "Are you all right? Open your eyes."
points: Responds: leave them as found if safe, find out what is wrong, get help, reassess regularly
No response: shout for help and go to the next step

steps.title: S – Send for help
steps.text: Call {EMERGENCY}, or get someone else to call. Use speakerphone so you keep your hands free and can follow the dispatcher's instructions.
points: Send someone to fetch an AED (defibrillator) if one may be nearby
Give your exact location – use the Location tool or nearby landmarks

steps.title: A – Airway
steps.text: Open the airway: one hand on the forehead, tilt the head back gently, lift the chin with two fingertips.
points: Look in the mouth only if you can see something blocking it – do not do blind finger sweeps

steps.title: B – Breathing
steps.text: Look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
points: Occasional gasps are NOT normal breathing – treat as not breathing
Not breathing normally: start CPR now
Breathing normally: check for bleeding and injuries, then place in the recovery position if unresponsive

action.label: Not breathing – go to Adult CPR

steps.title: C – Circulation / catastrophic bleeding
steps.text: Look quickly from head to toe for severe bleeding and control it with firm direct pressure. In an obvious catastrophic limb bleed, control bleeding first – even before airway and breathing.

steps.title: Trained responders: ABCDE
steps.text: If you are trained, continue a structured assessment, treating problems as you find them:
points: C – Circulation: bleeding, pulse, skin colour and temperature, capillary refill
D – Disability: level of response (AVPU – Alert, Voice, Pain, Unresponsive), pupils, blood glucose
E – Exposure: look for other injuries, keep them warm

steps.title: Keep reassessing
steps.text: Stay with the casualty. Check breathing and response regularly until help arrives, and note times and changes to hand over to responders.

doNot: Do not rush in to a dangerous scene
Do not move a casualty unless they are in immediate danger or you need to (for example to start CPR)
Do not give anything to eat or drink
Do not leave an unresponsive casualty alone unless you must to call for help
